title: audit-log-retention-tiering-and-pipeline-resilience-playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook documents the retention tiering, storage layout, and operational pipeline behavior for Redwood audit logs (auth, policy changes, admin actions, model access, SIEM exports). Goal: ensure queryability for 30d (hot), 365d (warm), and 7y (cold/archival), support legal holds/evidence automation, and provide clear backfill and failure-mode runbooks for operators.

Overview of retention tiers and rationale:
- Hot tier (0-30 days): low-latency index for incident response and realtime detections. Indexed into daily indices, full field mappings, retained on ES/Opensearch or managed cluster. Retention TTL: 30 days.
- Warm tier (31-365 days): compressed indices, slower hardware, queryable for audits and monthly compliance requests. Indices rolled to larger time-based shards (weekly). Retention TTL: 365 days.
- Cold tier (366 days - 7 years): raw event objects stored in cold S3 buckets (s3://redwood-audit-archive/) in compressed columnar format (Parquet/GZIP) with partitioning by year/month/customer-id. Read-path is via rehydrate + reindex or query-through-presto layer.
- Evidence/Legal hold: items can be pinned to retain beyond standard TTL. Legal holds create a metadata marker in the evidence catalog (evidence-db) and set retention-exempt flag on object(s).

Storage layout and identifiers:
- Raw events are written as newline-delimited JSON to S3 under s3://redwood-audit-raw/ingest-date=YYYY-MM-DD/partition=N/event.jsonl
- Each event contains mandatory top-level fields: event_id, ts_utc, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, schema_version. Schema v2 adds fields: actor_ip, client_app_id, auth_method, outcome_code, device_context.
- ES/OpenSearch indices are named: audit-hot-YYYY.MM.DD and audit-warm-YYYY.WW. Cold files use partition: year=YYYY/month=MM/tenant=ID.

Indexing strategy and schema considerations:
- Hot indexing: realtime ingest via logpipe -> kafka -> log-consumer -> es-bulk. Use daily indices with rollover when >50GB. Shard count: heuristic based on tenant cardinality; default 1 primary + 1 replica for small tenants, scaled for large tenants.
- Mappings: explicit mappings for critical fields (event_id keyword, ts_utc date, tenant_id keyword, action keyword, resource_id keyword) to avoid expensive dynamic mappings. Text fields (message, details) use subfield 'keyword' for aggregations.
- Nested fields avoided where possible; instead flatten keys with dot notation to improve query performance.
- Schema migrations: maintain mapping templates in repo; when schema_version increments, consumers MUST be able to accept both vN and vN+1. Backfill pipeline handles reindexing when mappings change.

Backfill and reindex process (high-level):
1) Identify scope: by date range and/or tenant; create backfill ticket with expected size, SLA, runbook link.
2) Snapshot raw artifacts: ensure raw event files for date range exist in s3://redwood-audit-raw/.
3) Dry-run transformation: run backfill-runner --dry-run --from YYYY-MM-DD --to YYYY-MM-DD --tenant <id> to surface mapping conflicts.
4) Create temporary indexing cluster or throttle to low-priority workers. Run backfill-runner with controlled concurrency: backfill-runner --from --to --concurrency 8 --batch-size 1000 --transform-script transforms/upgrade-schema-v2.js
5) Monitor reindex metrics (docs indexed/s, error rate, queue length).
6) Validate: run sampling queries against target indices; check for field presence, timestamp continuity, event counts.
7) Mark ticket complete and emit audit event backfill.completed with metadata.

Idempotency and deduplication:
- Events carry event_id generated by producer. Pipeline deduplicates by event_id at consumer checkpoint. Backfill process must skip events already present (use event_id-based upsert).
- For reindexes, use es-reindex with scripts that set op_type to create to avoid overwriting unless forced.

Failure modes and mitigation:
1) Ingestion lag (kafka backlog grows):
   - Causes: consumer crashes, GC pauses, broker issues.
   - Detect: alert when consumer lag > 1M messages or avg lag > 15m.
   - Mitigation: restart consumer with --reset-cursors, scale workers, or enable temporary burst capacity. If consumer repeatedly OOMs, toggle to single-threaded safe mode and open a PG for memory tuning.
2) Mapping conflicts (schema drift during rollouts):
   - Causes: new field emitted as object vs keyword, dynamic mapping picks wrong type.
   - Detect: mapping_conflict metrics in logpipe, index rejected documents > 0.
   - Mitigation: push mapping template patch, run backfill of affected date ranges, apply mapping change via index-template that migrates via reindex API. Create a block list for dynamic fields.
3) Poison messages on backfill (corrupt JSON or extreme size):
   - Detect: parsing error rate spikes, backfill-runner logs show failure on particular file key.
   - Mitigation: quarantine S3 object (move to s3://redwood-audit-quarantine/) and raise ticket to investigate. If only a few events, extract valid events and reprocess.
4) ES cluster disk pressure / shard failures:
   - Detect: disk.watermark, red/ yellow indices.
   - Mitigation: freeze older indices (move to warm), increase replica allocation, add ephemeral nodes, or pause indexing. If corruption, restore from snapshot.
5) SIEM export failures (downstream rate limits / timeouts):
   - Causes: SIEM endpoint throttling, network timeouts, malformed payloads.
   - Mitigation: exponential backoff with jitter; batch smaller payloads; maintain per-tenant pacing; fallback to buffered S3 export and async retry consumer.

Observability and SLOs:
- Key metrics: events/sec (in), events/sec (indexed), consumer_lag, indexing_error_rate, backfill_progress_pct, siem_export_success_rate.
- Alerts: consumer_lag > 30m (P1), indexing_error_rate > 0.5% sustained (P1), backfill failure (P2).
- Dashboards: Hot index latency heatmap, partition fill by tenant, SIEM export success per destination, legal-holds in effect.

Operational runbook snippets:
- Restart consumer safely:
  rctl service restart log-consumer --env=prod --grace=300
  wait-for-logpipe-ready --timeout=600
- Start a controlled backfill (example):
  backfill-runner --from 2023-11-01 --to 2023-11-30 --concurrency 4 --batch-size 2000 --tenant all --transform transforms/upgrade-schema-v2.js --es-target audit-warm-2023.11
- Quarantine corrupt file:
  aws s3 mv s3://redwood-audit-raw/ingest-date=2023-11-05/batch-0007.jsonl s3://redwood-audit-quarantine/2023-11-05-batch-0007.jsonl
- Rehydrate cold data for ad-hoc query:
  rehydrate-tool --s3-path s3://redwood-audit-archive/year=2021/month=06/tenant=acct-123 --to /tmp/rehydrate-202106 --format parquet

Evidence automation and legal holds:
- Evidence automation listens to evidence-db; when an evidence case is created, a job tags relevant S3 partitions and locks the ES/Warm indices by setting an index.metadata.legal_hold=true flag. The retention agent ignores indices/partitions with that flag.
- RBAC v2 integration: only principals in role 'forensics-analyst' and 'legal-admin' can create holds; toggles are audited in the same audit stream (action: evidence.hold.create).
- When a hold is released, a release ticket with justification must be created and the release action is recorded in audit logs.

SIEM export considerations:
- Exports should be delivered in NDJSON compressed payloads with batch size <= 10k events or 5MB per POST to respect partner limits.
- Rate throttling: use token-bucket per-destination. Track last-successful-offset so restarts resume without duplication.
- Transform rules: flatten sensitive fields before exporting (PII redaction rules) based on tenant policy. Redaction rules are keyed by tenant_id and stored in secrets manager.

Compliance checklist before doing a retention or pipeline change:
- Confirm schema changes are documented in Confluence and have migration PR with tests.
- Notify legal/compliance for retention changes beyond 1 year for regulated tenants.
- Run storage cost impact analysis and patch billing forecasts.
- Ensure snapshot schedule covers target indices (daily snapshots retained per retention policy).

Open action items / follow-ups:
- (SEC-OPEN-1) Finish automation for index freezing and warm relocation (owner: Marcus Chen).
- (SEC-OPEN-2) Implement a small-footprint ES reindex helper that does event_id-based upserts (owner: Ellen Rivera).
- (SEC-OPEN-3) Add SIEM export dashboard per-tenant (owner: Jonah Weiss).

Appendix: quick reference commands and locations:
- Raw S3: s3://redwood-audit-raw/
- Archive S3: s3://redwood-audit-archive/
- Quarantine S3: s3://redwood-audit-quarantine/
- Backfill tool: repo: github.com/redwood-inference/log-pipeline, binary: backfill-runner
- Consumer: service name log-consumer (k8s namespace: audit-prod)
- Evidence DB: postgres://evidence-db.redwood.internal:5432/evidence

Notes / informal troubleshooting tips (team scratchpad):
- If you see a sudden spike in indexing_error_rate after a deploy, suspect dynamic mapping change from a new client. Rollback template, run small reindex.
- For large backfills, pre-warm the target cluster with empty indices to avoid shard allocation skew.
- Keep an eye on tenant cardinality — high-cardinality fields are the most common cause of slow queries and disk blowouts. Consider moving those to the cold store or redacting them in the hot index.

End of playbook.
